content.title: How to watch Deontay Wilder vs. Derek Chisora fight: Time, PPV, full card, streaming details
content.text: Deontay Wilder reacts during a weigh in at York Hall, London, Friday April 3, 2026. (Adam Davy/PA via AP)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Dustin Hockensmith | dhockensmith@pennlive.comDeontay Wilder returns to the ring Saturday in London for his 50th career fight and a heavyweight battle against Derek Chisora. The card is scheduled to start at 2 p.m. ET (7 p.m. BST) with coverage on DAZN Pay-Per-View. Walkouts for the Wilder vs. Chisora fight are tentatively scheduled for 5:26 p.m. ET at O2 Arena in London, England.How to watch: Live streams of the Wilder vs. Chisora fight are available with DAZN Pay-Per-View. The cost is $49.99.Deontay Wilder (44-4-1, 43 KOs) vs. Derek Chisora (36-16, 23 KOs)The pennlive.com logoA subscription is required to read this story.Subscribe now to continue.Heavyweight contest at a glanceWhen: Saturday, April 4 at 2 p.m. ET (7 p.m. BST)Where: O2 Arena, London, EnglandTV channel: N/ALive stream: DAZN Pay-Per-View ($49.99)Wilder carries a 44-4-1 career record with 43 knockouts into this fight, but he has lost back-to-back fights to Zhilei Zhang in June 2024 and Joseph Parker in December 2023. He was also knocked out twice by Tyson Fury in 2020 and ‘21, respectively, which effectively put the 40-year-old’s career on the ropes.Wilder vs. Chisora live stream: DAZN Pay-Per-View ($49.99)Chisora, 42, hails from the United Kingdom and goes into Saturday’s fight with a 36-13-0 career record and 23 knockouts. He stands five-plus inches shorter than Wilder and also has losses to Fury and Parker on his ledger, but enters this fight having won three straight. Most recently, Chisora defeated Otto Wallin by unanimous decision last February after winning back-to-back fights in this same arena. The full scheduled fight card is as follows:Main event: Deontay Wilder vs. Derek Chisora, 12 rounds, heavyweightsTitle fight: Viddal Riley vs. Mateusz Masternak (Cruiserweight)Title fight: Denzel Bentley vs. Endry Saavedra (Middleweight)Matty Harris vs. Franklin Ignatius (Heavyweight)Amir Anderson vs. Jordan Dujon (Middleweight)
